name: TrustArc
description: TrustArc provides privacy governance, cookie consent management, consent and preference management, assessments, data mapping, and individual-rights workflows.
agentUseSummary: TrustArc is unavailable as a Relay agent connection because the current Cookie Consent Manager External API exposes its sole inventory read only to ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN roles whose same authority can add and remove websites and initiate scans. The API also uses an onboarding-specific tenant host and short-lived support-provisioned bearer tokens. Relay will not store an overprivileged privacy-administration credential or infer an undocumented read-only scope.

blocked.label: Connect TrustArc
blocked.description: Relay exposes no TrustArc connection while the documented metadata read requires an account-wide administrative role with mutation authority.

blocked.label: Collect administrative credentials
blocked.description: Support-issued API keys, session tokens, short-lived bearer tokens, client credentials, tenant hosts, account IDs, and Consent Manager IDs are not collected.

blocked.label: Read privacy or tracker data
blocked.description: Tracker inventory, domains, seed URLs, identifiers, organizations, data collected, purposes, consent records, preferences, assessments, reports, exports, and individual-rights data remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Mutate TrustArc
blocked.description: Adding or removing websites, initiating scans, changing trackers, consent or preference actions, assessments, reports, and every other mutation remain provider-side.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary interfaces
blocked.description: Onboarding-specific hosts, alternate regional origins, internal Swagger, arbitrary queries, browser sessions, scraping, and undocumented requests are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No TrustArc action or credential path is exposed until a stable provider-operated API offers a least-privilege read-only role or scope, fixed verifiable origin rules, and renewable service credentials separated from website and scan mutations.

runtimeSupport.description: No wrapper is mounted because the tracker inventory read requires an administrative role that also authorizes CCM mutations.

providerSetup.blocker: TrustArc's current CCM External API documents one tracker-inventory GET requiring SUPER_ADMIN or ADMIN. Those roles also authorize website additions/removals and scan creation; the documentation does not define a read-only role or scope. The API origin is an onboarding-specific CCM host and bearer tokens are short-lived and issued through the portal, onboarding contact, or support.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep TrustArc unavailable and do not collect its administrative credentials or privacy data. Re-evaluate only if TrustArc publishes a least-privilege read-only role or scope, fixed tenant-origin verification rules, service-token renewal and revocation, stable response schemas, and an authority boundary that excludes website, scan, tracker, consent, assessment, report, and rights-request mutations.

evidence.supports: TrustArc documents an onboarding-specific CCM host, support- or portal-issued short-lived bearer tokens, and SUPER_ADMIN, ADMIN, or DESIGNER roles for the External API.

The official v1 reference documents website add/remove and scan creation mutations; its tracker inventory GET requires SUPER_ADMIN or ADMIN and exposes tracker domains, identifiers, organizations, collected data, and purposes.
TrustArc's separate API token guide documents client-credentials bearer tokens whose response includes account and user identity fields, without establishing a CCM tracker-read-only scope.
